title: Microsoft Purview DLP: stop Copilot sending sensitive data to external web search
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, governance paths, commands and opt-in enforcement are supported. Licensing for the web-search action remains explicitly unconfirmed, and the briefing preserves the documented Cowork and domain-exclusion limitations.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-06-12T22:00:47.
When web search is enabled, Copilot can send a query derived from the prompt to its web search provider.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: The web-search DLP protection is a real-time control.
claims.quote: This real-time control helps organizations mitigate data leakage and oversharing risks

claims.claim: The web-search rule detects configured sensitive information types, including custom SITs, in prompt text.
claims.quote: When a prompt contains sensitive information types (SITs)—such as credit card numbers, passport numbers, Social Security numbers, or custom SITs defined by your organization

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The web-search action is Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.
claims.quote: In the same rule, set the action to **Prevent Copilot from processing content** > **Performing Web Searches**.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: A matching web-search rule blocks external web grounding for that prompt and prevents matched prompt text reaching the search provider.
claims.quote: This prevents prompt text that matches the configured SITs from being sent to external search providers for that request.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment
claims.claim: The web-search-only restriction still permits responses grounded in internal Microsoft 365 data the user may access.
claims.quote: Copilot still returns a response grounded in internal Microsoft 365 data sources where the user has access.

claims.claim: The web-search DLP action covers Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat and Cowork.
claims.quote: **Restrict Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork from using external web search when prompts contain sensitive data.**

claims.claim: The capability extends to Copilot Studio agents published to Microsoft 365 Copilot.
claims.quote: This capability currently extends to Microsoft 365 Copilot and agents built in Copilot Studio that are published to Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: The same Copilot DLP location can prevent labelled files and emails from being used in response summaries.
claims.quote: Identified items still appear in the citations of the response, but Copilot and Cowork don't access or use the content of the item in the response.

claims.claim: The location also supports blocking sensitive prompts instead of only their web grounding.
claims.quote: This policy prevents Copilot and Cowork from returning a response when prompts contain sensitive data.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The web-grounding restriction is admin-opt-in rather than enforced by default.
claims.quote:
The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding. Valid values are:

- $true: Web grounding is blocked.
- $False: Web grounding isn't blocked. This value is the default.

claims.claim: Microsoft Graph enforces existing security permissions on customer content.
claims.quote: It enforces the security permissions present on a customer’s content and provides secure, compliant, auditable access to that content.

claims.claim: Copilot prompts run in the security context of the initiating user.
claims.quote: All Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts run in the security context of the user who initiates the prompt.

claims.claim: DLP alerts are supported at the Copilot location.
claims.quote: DLP alerts and DLP notifications are supported.

claims.claim: DLP notifications are supported at the Copilot location.
claims.quote: DLP alerts and DLP notifications are supported.

claims.quote: Customizing the link in Copilot policy tips isn't yet supported for Cowork.

claims.claim: Simulation mode is available for testing Copilot DLP policies.
claims.quote: Policy simulation mode is available for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Cowork.

claims.claim: Copilot DLP policies can include or exclude users and groups.
claims.quote: Select the **Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork** location and choose the users and groups to include or exclude within the selected administrative units.

claims.claim: Administrative-unit support is preview, rolling out and potentially unavailable in a tenant.
claims.quote: Administrative unit support for this location, including Cowork, is in preview and is rolling out. The option might not yet be available in your tenant.

claims.claim: The Purview path is Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork.
claims.quote: Go to **Data Loss Prevention** > **Policies** and select **+ Create policy**. ... Select the **Custom** template, then **Custom policy**. ... On the **Locations** page, set the **Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork** location to on.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule accepts Name, Policy, ContentContainsSensitiveInformation with a SIT Name hashtable, and RestrictWebGrounding $true to block web grounding.
claims.quote:
New-DlpComplianceRule
    [-Name] <String>
    -Policy <PolicyIdParameter>
...
The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding. Valid values are:

- $true: Web grounding is blocked.

claims.claim: Purview Data Security AI Admin is one of the roles allowed to create or edit Copilot DLP policies.
claims.quote: **Purview Data Security AI Admin** - Role for editing Data Loss Prevention policies related to Copilot and viewing AI content in Data Security Posture Management.

claims.claim: Copilot DLP can be administered tenant-wide while allowing narrower user or administrative-unit targeting.
claims.quote: An unrestricted administrator can scope policies to administrative units or keep **Full directory** to apply a policy across the organization. Existing tenant-wide policies continue to apply; using administrative units is optional.

claims.claim: The Apps admin center path is Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings.
claims.quote: Under **Customization**, select **Policy Management**. ... On the **Policy configurations** page, select **Create**. ... On the **Start with the basics** page ... On the **Choose the scope** page ... On the **Configure Settings** page

claims.claim: The beta PATCH policySettings endpoint accepts the allowwebsearch setting identifier and a required string value body.
The Graph settings API supports tenant-level policies only, not group-level or user-level policies.
claims.quote: The API addresses settings individually by their identifier, and only tenant-level policies are supported. User-level and group-level policies aren't supported.

claims.claim: An admin UI for configuring this tenant domain-exclusion list is not yet documented.

claims.quote:
Create your domain exclusion configuration from a CSV file:

```powershell
   .\ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1 -Create -FromFile "input.csv"
```

claims.quote: To manage the Copilot domain exclusion configuration for your tenant, use the **ConfigureTenantDomainExclusions.ps1** PowerShell script.
